DISCRIMINANTS AND DIFFERENTS 16

8. The Dedekind different

0BW0 Let \(A \to B\) be a ring map. We say the Dedekind different is defined if \(A\) is Noetherian, \(A \to B\) is finite, any nonzerodivisor on \(A\) is a nonzerodivisor on \(B\), and \(K \to L\) is étale where \(K = Q(A)\) and \(L = B \otimes_A K\). Then \(K \subset L\) is finite étale and
\[
\mathcal{L}_{B/A}=\{x\in L \mid \mathrm{Trace}_{L/K}(bx)\in A \text{ for all } b\in B\}
\]
is the Dedekind complementary module. In this situation the Dedekind different is
\[
\mathfrak{D}_{B/A}=\{x\in L \mid x\mathcal{L}_{B/A}\subset B\}
\]
viewed as a \(B\)-submodule of \(L\). By Lemma 8.1 the Dedekind different is an ideal of \(B\) either if \(A\) is normal or if \(B\) is flat over \(A\).

0BW1 Lemma 8.1. Assume the Dedekind different of \(A \to B\) is defined. Consider the statements

(1) \(A \to B\) is flat,  
(2) \(A\) is a normal ring,  
(3) \(\mathrm{Trace}_{L/K}(B)\subset A\),  
(4) \(1\in \mathcal{L}_{B/A}\), and  
(5) the Dedekind different \(\mathfrak{D}_{B/A}\) is an ideal of \(B\).

0BW2 Lemma 8.2. If the Dedekind different of \(A \to B\) is defined, then there is a canonical isomorphism \(\mathcal{L}_{B/A} \to \omega_{B/A}\).

Proof. Recall that \(\omega_{B/A}=\mathrm{Hom}_A(B,A)\) as \(A \to B\) is finite. We send \(x\in \mathcal{L}_{B/A}\) to the map \(b\mapsto \mathrm{Trace}_{L/K}(bx)\). Conversely, given an \(A\)-linear map \(\varphi: B \to A\) we obtain a \(K\)-linear map \(\varphi_K: L \to K\). Since \(K \to L\) is finite étale, we see that the trace pairing is nondegenerate (Lemma 3.1) and hence there exists a \(x\in L\) such that \(\varphi_K(y)=\mathrm{Trace}_{L/K}(xy)\) for all \(y\in L\). Then \(x\in \mathcal{L}_{B/A}\) maps to \(\varphi\) in \(\omega_{B/A}\). \(\square\)

0BW3 Lemma 8.3. If the Dedekind different of \(A \to B\) is defined and \(A \to B\) is flat, then

(1) the canonical isomorphism \(\mathcal{L}_{B/A} \to \omega_{B/A}\) sends \(1\in \mathcal{L}_{B/A}\) to the trace element \(\tau_{B/A}\in \omega_{B/A}\), and  
(2) the Dedekind different is \(\mathfrak{D}_{B/A}=\{b\in B \mid b\omega_{B/A}\subset B\tau_{B/A}\}\).

Proof. The first assertion follows from the proof of Lemma 8.1 and Lemma 4.3. The second assertion is immediate from the first and the definitions. \(\square\)

## 49.8 The Dedekind different

Let $A \to B$ be a ring map. We say the Dedekind different is defined if $A$ is Noetherian, $A \to B$ is finite, any nonzerodivisor on $A$ is a nonzerodivisor on $B$, and $K \to L$ is étale where $K = Q(A)$ and $L = B \otimes _ A K$. Then $K \subset L$ is finite étale and

\[ \mathcal{L}_{B/A} = \{ x \in L \mid \text{Trace}_{L/K}(bx) \in A \text{ for all }b \in B\} \]

is the Dedekind complementary module. In this situation the Dedekind different is

\[ \mathfrak {D}_{B/A} = \{ x \in L \mid x\mathcal{L}_{B/A} \subset B\} \]

viewed as a $B$-submodule of $L$. By Lemma 49.8.1 the Dedekind different is an ideal of $B$ either if $A$ is normal or if $B$ is flat over $A$.

Lemma 49.8.1. Assume the Dedekind different of $A \to B$ is defined. Consider the statements

  1. $A \to B$ is flat,

  2. $A$ is a normal ring,

  3. $\text{Trace}_{L/K}(B) \subset A$,

  4. $1 \in \mathcal{L}_{B/A}$, and

  5. the Dedekind different $\mathfrak {D}_{B/A}$ is an ideal of $B$.

Lemma 49.8.2. If the Dedekind different of $A \to B$ is defined, then there is a canonical isomorphism $\mathcal{L}_{B/A} \to \omega _{B/A}$.

Proof. Recall that $\omega _{B/A} = \mathop{\mathrm{Hom}}\nolimits _ A(B, A)$ as $A \to B$ is finite. We send $x \in \mathcal{L}_{B/A}$ to the map $b \mapsto \text{Trace}_{L/K}(bx)$. Conversely, given an $A$-linear map $\varphi : B \to A$ we obtain a $K$-linear map $\varphi _ K : L \to K$. Since $K \to L$ is finite étale, we see that the trace pairing is nondegenerate (Lemma 49.3.1) and hence there exists a $x \in L$ such that $\varphi _ K(y) = \text{Trace}_{L/K}(xy)$ for all $y \in L$. Then $x \in \mathcal{L}_{B/A}$ maps to $\varphi $ in $\omega _{B/A}$. $\square$

Lemma 49.8.3. If the Dedekind different of $A \to B$ is defined and $A \to B$ is flat, then

  1. the canonical isomorphism $\mathcal{L}_{B/A} \to \omega _{B/A}$ sends $1 \in \mathcal{L}_{B/A}$ to the trace element $\tau _{B/A} \in \omega _{B/A}$, and

  2. the Dedekind different is $\mathfrak {D}_{B/A} = \{ b \in B \mid b\omega _{B/A} \subset B\tau _{B/A}\} $.

Proof. The first assertion follows from the proof of Lemma 49.8.1 and Lemma 49.4.3. The second assertion is immediate from the first and the definitions. $\square$

L22: 【8†Lemma 49.7.4.】 Let $A$ be a ring. Let $n \geq 1$ and $f_1, \ldots , f_ n \in A[x_1, \ldots , x_ n]$. Set $B = A[x_1, \ldots , x_ n]/(f_1, \ldots , f_ n)$. The Kähler different of $B$ over $A$ is the ideal of $B$ generated by $\det (\partial f_ i/\partial x_ j)$.
L23: 
L24: Proof. This is true because $\Omega _{B/A}$ has a presentation
L25: 
L26: \[ \bigoplus \nolimits _{i = 1, \ldots , n} B f_ i \xrightarrow {\text{d}} \bigoplus \nolimits _{j = 1, \ldots , n} B \text{d}x_ j \rightarrow \Omega _{B/A} \rightarrow 0 \]
L27: by Algebra, Lemma 【14†10.131.9】. $\square$

L22: 【8†Lemma 15.24.20.】 Let $A$ be a Noetherian normal domain with fraction field $K$. Let $L$ be a finite extension of $K$. If the integral closure $B$ of $A$ in $L$ is finite over $A$, then $B$ is reflexive as an $A$-module.
L23: Proof. It suffices to show that $B = \bigcap B_\mathfrak p$ where the intersection is over height $1$ primes $\mathfrak p \subset A$, see Lemma 【14†15.24.18】. Let $b \in \bigcap B_\mathfrak p$. Let $x^ d + a_1x^{d - 1} + \ldots + a_ d$ be the minimal polynomial of $b$ over $K$. We want to show $a_ i \in A$. By Algebra, Lemma 【15†10.38.6】 we see that $a_ i \in A_\mathfrak p$ for all $i$ and all height one primes $\mathfrak p$.
L24: Hence we get what we want from Algebra, Lemma 【16†10.157.6】 (or the lemma already cited as $A$ is a reflexive module over itself). $\square$
